question: According to an article by Politico1, the WHO recommends making Ozempic-like drugs available to everyone, not just the wealthy. The active ingredient semaglutide, Ozempic’s chief component, is primarily used to treat type 2 diabetes. The WHO’s guidelines2 recommend extending the use of GLP-1 therapies to the long-term treatment of adult obesity. 1.
Will Ozempic and similar or related medicines also be approved as weight loss drugs in the EU, or will they remain chiefly for the treatment of diabetes?
Will a medical prescription for the treatment of diabetes be required to purchase Ozempic?
Will Ozempic and similar medicines be available more cheaply in the EU, and if so, for the treatment of which conditions?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (30.1.2026) On 8 February 2018, the medicinal product Ozempic (active substance semaglutide) was granted a marketing authorisation valid across the European Union1. Ozempic is indicated for the treatment of adults with insufficiently controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus as an adjunct to diet and exercise2.

Related medicinal products, namely Saxenda (liraglutide)3, Wegovy (semaglutide)4 and Mounjaro (tirzepatide)5 were granted EU marketing authorisations on 23 March 20156, 6 January 20227 and 15 September 20228, respectively. They are indicated to help manage weight along with diet and increased physical activity.

The active substances semaglutide, liraglutide and tirzepatide are all glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor antagonists. Tirzepatide has an additional mechanism of action as it also targets GIP (glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide) receptors.

As indicated in the publicly available product information for Ozempic (page 29)9, Saxenda (page 25)10, Wegovy (pag 33)11 and Mounjaro (pag 40)12, all these medicinal products are subject to medical prescription.

The Commission has no competence to reply on the question whether Ozempic or Ozempicsimilar medicines will become more affordable and under which conditions, as decisions on pricing and reimbursement of medicines are a competence and responsibility of the Member States according to Article 168(7) of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union.
